title: How to Lead a Parish Group on a Kibeho Pilgrimage in Rwanda
meta_title: Kibeho Pilgrimage, Rwanda: Feast Days, Stays and Travel
meta_description: Planning a Kibeho pilgrimage for a parish group? Feast dates, the drive from Kigali, where to sleep and how to add Nyungwe or gorillas in Rwanda.
excerpt: A Kibeho pilgrimage takes a parish group to Africa's only Vatican-approved Marian shrine in southern Rwanda. Here is how to choose the date, handle feast-day crowds and add Nyungwe, Lake Kivu or the gorillas.
content:
A Kibeho pilgrimage takes a parish or prayer group to the Shrine of Our Lady of Kibeho in Nyaruguru District, southern Rwanda, where the Catholic Church recognises Marian apparitions reported between 1981 and 1989. Most groups fly into Kigali, drive about four hours south, and spend one or two nights near the shrine.

The hard part for a group leader is not the faith side, which your priest or chaplain will shape, but everything around it: feast days when every bed in the area is taken, a long road day with older pilgrims, and whether to add Nyungwe Forest or the gorillas afterwards. This guide covers dates, the drive, rooming, vehicles, safety and a sample week, and our club and faith group safaris page shows how we put the ground arrangements together for organised groups.

Quick Facts

  • Where: Kibeho, Nyaruguru District, Southern Province, in the Catholic Diocese of Butare
  • Drive from Kigali: about four hours by road
  • Main feast days: 28 November (anniversary of the first apparition, with a vigil on 27 November) and 15 August (Assumption)
  • Church recognition: declared authentic by the local bishop in 2001, the only Vatican-approved Marian apparition site in Africa
  • Visa: single-entry tourist visa on arrival US$50; East Africa Tourist Visa for Rwanda, Uganda and Kenya US$100 (checked November 2026)
  • Altitude: southern Rwanda sits at roughly 1,800 metres, so evenings are cool
  • Good add-ons: Nyungwe Forest, Lake Kivu and, for pilgrims aged 15 and over, gorilla trekking

What Is the Kibeho Pilgrimage, and Why Do Parish Groups Go?

The Kibeho pilgrimage is a journey to the place where three schoolgirls at Kibeho College said the Virgin Mary appeared to them, beginning on 28 November 1981. Mary is honoured there as Nyina wa Jambo, Mother of the Word, and the shrine draws pilgrims from across Africa, Europe, Asia and the Americas.

The three visionaries the Church recognises are Alphonsine Mumureke, Anathalie Mukamazimpaka and Marie Claire Mukangango. Alphonsine's visions began on 28 November 1981 and ended on the same date in 1989; Anathalie's ran from early 1982 to December 1983, and Marie Claire's lasted through much of 1982. The messages called for prayer, conversion and repentance, and the shrine is closely tied to the Rosary of the Seven Sorrows of Mary.

The Church's approval and what it means for your group

Bishop Augustin Misago of Butare declared the apparitions to the three seers authentic in 2001, and the Holy See confirmed his judgement. For a parish group this matters in practical ways: the shrine runs an organised calendar of Masses and devotions, and at the 2025 anniversary vigil the readings were given in Kinyarwanda, French and English. If you want your own priest to concelebrate or say a private Mass for the group, ask the shrine well in advance.

Kibeho also carries the weight of Rwanda's history, so a thoughtful Kibeho pilgrimage makes room for remembrance as well as celebration.

When Should a Group Make the Kibeho Pilgrimage?

The best time for a Kibeho pilgrimage depends on what your group wants: the anniversary on 28 November and the Assumption on 15 August offer the most moving liturgies but enormous crowds, while an ordinary weekday in June to September gives quiet prayer time, dry roads and easy beds. Most parish leaders choose between atmosphere and comfort.

TimingWhat happens at KibehoWhat it means for a group
27-28 NovemberVigil Mass on the 27th, then the Seven Sorrows chaplet, catechesis and a solemn festive Mass on the 28thBook rooms 9-12 months ahead; expect walking from a drop-off point and long outdoor services
15 August (Assumption)The largest gathering of the year, with crowds in the tens of thousandsDry season, so roads are easy, but water, toilets and food queues are stretched
June-September, other datesDaily Masses and devotions with far smaller numbersBest for older pilgrims and groups who want unhurried prayer and a private Mass
March-MayRwanda's long rains; services continue as normalQuietest and easiest to book, but muddy paths and slower drives; pack rain jackets
Holy Week and EasterNot one of the shrine's two great feasts; check its programme for the weekWorks for groups that want Easter liturgies in Kigali and a quieter shrine visit

Crowd sizes on feast days are large. On the eve of the Assumption in 2023, the shrine's director of pilgrims told KT Press that more than 30,000 people had already arrived, and earlier years have seen far bigger figures. If your Kibeho pilgrimage falls on 28 November this year, assume every room near the shrine has gone and plan to stay further away.

Is the 28 November feast worth the crowds?

For many groups, yes: praying among Rwandan families and choirs on the anniversary itself is the high point of a Kibeho pilgrimage. The trade-off is comfort, as the services are outdoors and long. Groups with frail members often attend the vigil on the 27th, or visit a few days later.

How Long Is the Drive From Kigali to Kibeho?

The road trip from Kigali to Kibeho takes about four hours on tarmac for most of the way, heading south through Muhanga and Huye before the final stretch into Nyaruguru. Groups usually leave Kigali after breakfast, stop for lunch in Huye and reach the shrine in time for afternoon prayers or a late-day Mass.

A recent opinion piece in the New Times described smoother, better-managed traffic into Kibeho on Assumption Day 2026 after government investment in the Nyaruguru road. That helps, but on feast days police control access and coaches may stop well short of the shrine, so pilgrims should be fit for a walk of a kilometre or two.

Worthwhile stops on the way

On a Kibeho pilgrimage, Huye, the old university town once called Butare, makes a natural lunch and comfort stop and has the country's national ethnographic museum. Kigali Genocide Memorial in the capital is the usual first visit for groups who want to understand Rwanda before they travel south. Murambi Genocide Memorial in Nyamagabe District, one of four memorial sites added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2023, lies on the road west from Huye towards Nyungwe and fits the day you leave Kibeho.

These memorials are hard visits, so brief the group beforehand and leave a quiet evening afterwards.

Where Does a Pilgrim Group Sleep Near the Shrine?

A group on a Kibeho pilgrimage sleeps either in the church-run guesthouses and small hotels in Kibeho itself, or in Huye, the nearest larger town, with a morning drive to the shrine. On feast days the shrine does not allow sleeping on its grounds, and hotels, guesthouses and host families nearby fill completely.

Staying in Kibeho means early Masses on foot and evening prayer without a coach transfer, the full rhythm of a Kibeho pilgrimage. The trade-off is simpler rooms and stretched service on big days: a first-hand account in the New Times from Assumption Day 2026 described understaffed breakfasts and closed kitchens at two of the Kibeho hotels under feast-day pressure. Huye has a wider choice of hotels with reliable hot water and dining rooms that can seat a whole group together.

Rooming a parish group

On a Kibeho pilgrimage most parish groups share twin rooms, with single rooms kept for the priest, the group leader and anyone who needs one for health reasons. Ask for ground-floor rooms for pilgrims who struggle with stairs, and keep the group in one property if you can, because splitting a group across hotels doubles the morning headcount problem. On a feast date, a single property able to hold 25 to 30 people near the shrine is rare, which is why we often base larger groups in Huye.

Group Logistics: Vehicles, Pricing Logic and Safety

Group logistics for a Kibeho pilgrimage come down to three decisions: the right vehicle for your numbers, a clear understanding of what drives the per-person price, and a safety plan for crowds. Getting these right early is what makes the spiritual programme run on time.

Vehicles by group size

Group sizeUsual vehicleNotes
Up to 6One safari 4x4 or a comfortable minivanThe same vehicle can continue to Nyungwe or the Virungas
7-14A minibus, or two 4x4s if you add AkageraKeep a spare seat for bags and for anyone who needs to stretch a leg
15-30A coaster-style bus with a driver-guide and a second escortBig buses may be stopped further from the shrine on feast days
30+Two coasters, each with its own guideSplit into two named sub-groups with their own meeting points

What drives the price per pilgrim

The per-person cost of a Kibeho pilgrimage falls as more people share a vehicle, a guide and a chaplain's room, and rises sharply on feast dates when the few rooms near the shrine command a premium. Single rooms, fly-in transfers and gorilla permits are fixed per person, so they do not get cheaper with numbers. A private Kibeho pilgrimage lets you choose your dates and pace, keep your own priest with you and hold Mass on your schedule, which you cannot do when you join strangers on a shared tour.

Safety and paperwork

Rwanda is one of the most orderly countries in the region, and the police manage feast-day crowds calmly. For the 2025 anniversary the shrine asked every pilgrim to carry identification and health insurance documents, and advised pregnant women and people with health conditions to think carefully about the crowds. It also warned that it never asks for money through random phone calls, so treat any "Kibeho project" fundraising call as a scam.

On a Kibeho pilgrimage, give every pilgrim a card with the hotel name, the guide's number and a fixed meeting point. Check entry rules on the Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration website before you travel, as visa fees change.

A Sample 7-Day Kibeho Pilgrimage With Nyungwe and Lake Kivu

A seven-day Kibeho pilgrimage gives a group two nights near the shrine, a day of rest in Nyungwe Forest and two nights on Lake Kivu before the drive back to Kigali. It keeps road days under five hours and leaves room for a private Mass, the Stations of the Cross and the Seven Sorrows rosary at the shrine.

DayPlanOvernight
1Arrive in Kigali; evening Mass at a city parish or quiet time after the flightKigali
2Kigali Genocide Memorial in the morning, then the drive south via HuyeKibeho or Huye
3A full day at the shrine: Mass, the apparition site, the Seven Sorrows rosary and time for confessionKibeho or Huye
4Morning prayer at Kibeho, then west past Murambi to the edge of Nyungwe ForestNyungwe
5Optional early chimpanzee tracking or the canopy walk; afternoon drive to Lake KivuLake Kivu
6A rest day by the lake, a boat trip and a closing Mass for the groupLake Kivu
7Drive back to Kigali for evening flightsDeparture

Nyungwe is the obvious partner for a Kibeho pilgrimage because it lies on the same side of the country. The forest is home to chimpanzees and large troops of colobus monkeys, and the canopy walkway gives even non-hikers a view over the treetops. Our 8-day Rwanda primates and Lake Kivu trip follows a similar southern loop and can be rebuilt around shrine days, while the shorter Akagera and Nyungwe safari suits a group that wants savannah game as well.

Can Pilgrims Add Gorilla Trekking to the Trip?

Pilgrims can add gorilla trekking in Volcanoes National Park, in the north-west, if each trekker is at least 15 and fit for a steep, muddy walk. A permit costs US$1,500 per person (checked October 2026), so most groups offer it as an optional extension after the Kibeho pilgrimage.

From Lake Kivu, the drive north to Musanze takes most of a morning, so a gorilla extension adds two nights to the trip. Permits are booked through the Rwanda Development Board and sell out early in the dry months, which is why we secure them first and build the rest of the extension around the trekking date. Read our guide to the Rwanda gorilla permit for the booking rules, and our post on Rwanda in December if you are travelling around the November feast.

Those who skip the trek can enjoy a gentle day around Musanze instead. If your parish is weighing a Kibeho pilgrimage against other East African options, our guides to the Namugongo pilgrimage in Uganda and a church group trip to Kenya show how those trips differ.

Insider Tips for Group Leaders

  • Contact the shrine early: arrange your priest's concelebration or a private Mass before you fix the dates
  • Feast-day beds: for 28 November or 15 August, hold rooms close to a year ahead, or base the group in Huye
  • Dress: modest clothing covering shoulders and knees, sturdy shoes for walking, and a warm layer for cool evenings
  • Outdoor services: pack sun hats, rain jackets, refillable water bottles and a small cushion
  • Documents: passport, visa, travel insurance details and a printed hotel card for each pilgrim
  • Pace: keep road days under five hours and build in a quiet afternoon after the memorial visits
  • Live stream: family at home can follow the main feast-day ceremonies on the shrine's YouTube channel

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the Kibeho pilgrimage?

The Kibeho pilgrimage can be made on any day of the year, but the two great feast days are 28 November, the anniversary of the first apparition in 1981, and 15 August, the Assumption. Both draw very large crowds. Groups wanting quiet prayer and easy rooms choose an ordinary weekday in June to September.

How far is Kibeho from Kigali?

Kibeho is about four hours by road from Kigali, in Nyaruguru District in the far south of Rwanda. The usual route runs south through Muhanga and Huye, with lunch in Huye. On feast days, allow extra time, because police control traffic near the shrine and coaches may drop pilgrims a walk away from the main grounds.

Is Our Lady of Kibeho approved by the Catholic Church?

Our Lady of Kibeho is approved by the Catholic Church. In 2001 Bishop Augustin Misago of Butare declared the apparitions to Alphonsine Mumureke, Anathalie Mukamazimpaka and Marie Claire Mukangango authentic, and the Holy See confirmed the judgement. It is the only Vatican-approved Marian apparition site in Africa.

Where do pilgrims stay at Kibeho?

Pilgrims at Kibeho stay in church-run guesthouses and small hotels in the village, or in hotels in Huye, the nearest larger town. On feast days the shrine does not allow sleeping on its grounds and nearby rooms are fully booked well in advance, so large groups often base themselves in Huye and drive in each morning.

Can a Kibeho pilgrimage be combined with gorilla trekking?

A Kibeho pilgrimage combines well with gorilla trekking in Volcanoes National Park, though the park is in the north-west and needs two extra nights. Trekkers must be at least 15, and a Rwanda permit costs US$1,500 per person (checked October 2026). Many parish groups make the trek optional and plan a gentler Kigali day for those who stay behind.

Final Thoughts

A good Kibeho pilgrimage starts with one honest choice: the joy and crowds of a feast day, or the stillness of an ordinary week. Once the date is fixed, the rest follows: where you sleep, the size of the bus, and whether Nyungwe, Lake Kivu or the gorillas come afterwards.

If this November's feast is too close, now is the right time to start planning a Kibeho pilgrimage for the next one.
